requirements.requirement: On node1, create a 512 MiB swap file and activate it immediately.
requirements.summary: The /swapfile file is exactly 536,870,912 bytes (512 MiB), has a valid swap signature, and is directly shown in /proc/swaps as active.

requirements.requirement: Configure the swap file to activate after future boots.
requirements.summary: A valid /etc/fstab entry was present before restart. After node1 changed boot identity, /swapfile remained intact and was directly observed as an active systemd swap unit and in /proc/swaps; the system was running with no failed units.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates an active 512 MiB swap file, persistent configuration, a real node restart, and successful post-boot recovery. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively demonstrated and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The reboot command lost its SSH connection before printing its explicit acknowledgement marker. Nevertheless, the immediate disconnect, changed boot identity, eight-second uptime, and fixed lifecycle observations coherently demonstrate that the restart occurred.
Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, limiting independent package consistency assessment; the command timeline contains no package mutations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. File creation and permissions, swap initialization and activation, fstab persistence, the bounded swapon -a validation, and reboot all directly supported the required outcome or restart verification. The failed unprivileged display command was read-only and caused no demonstrated harm. Post-run observations show no failed services, new exposure, or executor-created temporary residue; socket and systemd-private-directory changes are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
